identity.name: DHFR replica ensembles on one GPU: sequential versus concurrent MPS

found_evidence: Public upstream executable benchmark.py, input PDB and force fields verified accessible. NVIDIA publishes the CUDA pme command. Supplied brief provides the exact fixed-work driver and command; this driver is an adaptation, not an independently published ensemble result.

outcome_definition.scientific: Per-replica mean and final potential energy in kJ/mol from 100 samples at steps 250 through 25000; brief additionally requests equality of the full sampled energy series.
outcome_definition.performance: Total wall seconds for fixed ensemble; aggregate simulated ns/day = 0.8 * 86400 / total_wall_s; speedup = sequential_total_wall_s / concurrent_total_wall_s.

citations.role: Independent published MPS measurements and executable command

source_licences_and_intended_use.intended_use: Local execution, benchmarking and modification; no redistribution planned.

stock_cuda_image.reason: Stock image manifest, Python version, architecture, GPU model, driver and MPS availability are unspecified; no reproduction performed.
provisional_feasibility_evidence: PyPI provides Linux x86_64 glibc 2.27/2.28 OpenMM 8.2.0 wheels for CPython 3.10 through 3.13 and a CUDA 12 plugin wheel.
CUDA plugin declares NVIDIA CUDA 12 runtime, NVCC, NVRTC, CUPTI and cuFFT dependencies.
NVIDIA study used OpenMM 8.2.0, CUDA 12 and Python 3.12; describes regular-user MPS startup on Volta or newer GPUs.
requirements: One CUDA 12 compatible NVIDIA GPU and host driver
MPS executable and support for sharing GPU between processes

memory.scope: One shared PDB (1814203 bytes) plus amber99sb.xml (467697) and tip3p.xml (891), excluding software.
memory.reason: No published host/device peak working set for the fixed eight-replica workload; not measured.

scientific_checks: Eight distinct replicas, seeds 1000 through 1007, 25000 steps each.
Compare per-replica mean and final potential energies; full-series comparison requires additional output from the supplied driver.
scoring.reason: NVIDIA provides throughput observations, not acceptance criteria for this fixed-work adaptation. Brief predictions are hypotheses, not independently published anchors.
scoring.fallback_variation_rule: Brief suggests same-seed sequential run-to-run variation if not bit-identical; no numerical variation or statistical rule supplied.

repeatability.reason: Brief specifies fixed seeds but no repeat count or statistical aggregation.
repeatability.limitations: CUDA deterministic force calculation is documented, not validated here. Same-seed full trajectory identity across process arrangements remains an untested hypothesis. CPU PME determinism cannot be assumed.

search_note: No benchmark search performed; only supplied sources and their pinned public data inspected.
